To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) Gold-style learning and query learning are closely related; (ii) the relations depend on the structure of the target classes; (iii) the enumerability of target classes is not crucial for these relations; (iv) the relations are not due to the recursiveness of target languages; and (v) the relations do not hold in general for non-recursive target languages.
Gold-style and query learners can be interchanged for learning arbitrary classes of recursive languages and that this is not true in general for arbitrary classes of recursively-enumerable languages.

Gold-style learning and query learning can be related in a very general setting, but that this relation is not always symmetric, and that the relation is affected by the algorithmic properties of the target class.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: What are the differences between language learning from examples (Gold-style) and from queries?
the question how general the relationships between Gold-style and learning from queries are.
a comparison of two approaches to language identification from examples and queries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relations between Gold-style learning and query learning hold for arbitrary recursive classes, but that they are no longer valid for arbitrary recursive enumerable classes.
Gold-style and query learners are equally powerful, but the latter type of learners is not a generalization of the former type.
Gold-style and query learners have different capabilities in general, but that there are significant relationships in some cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in general, the learning capabilities in the two approaches are not equivalent, but that the relations between the approaches are determined by properties of the target class.
the 'equality' between Gold-style and learning from queries holds, if the target class is enumerable, but not if it is non-enumerable.
Gold-style learning and query learning are very different, but in many settings they are closely related.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the recursiveness or enumerability of the languages is crucial for Gold-style learning, but is irrelevant for query learning.
, even in the most general context of language learning, Gold-style and query learners have different learning capabilities, which are not due to the algorithmic properties of the target classes.
, even in the context of arbitrary classes of recursive languages the learning models of Gold-style and of query learning are still strongly related.
